title: Revocation Fail-Open via Remote Timeouts
pattern: Querying a remote service or database to check for credential revocation, but treating network timeouts, timeouts, or service unavailability as "valid".
why_bad: Attackers can exploit this behavior by executing a Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack against the revocation server, causing verification requests to fail or time out, which allows revoked credentials to pass unchecked.
detection: Network request wrappers in authentication logic that return `true` or a successful fallback status on connection timeout or status code errors.
fix: Default to failing closed if the revocation verification system cannot be reached, or rely on a locally cached, cryptographically signed revocation list.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 9, p. 201.
